stories.name: House Republicans elect Jim Jordan as their leader for the next Congress
facts: On Tuesday, Nov. 10, House Republicans who will serve in the next Congress chose Rep. Jim Jordan of Ohio, the Judiciary Committee chairman, to lead them in the minority, beating Majority Leader Steve Scalise of Louisiana 106 to 73 in a secret ballot at the Capitol.

The vote follows the party's midterm losses; Speaker Mike Johnson is stepping down from leadership. Democrats hold their leadership elections next week, with Hakeem Jeffries expected to become speaker.
After the vote Jordan gave brief remarks, saying House Republicans will fight for American families over the next two years.

people.name: Jim Jordan

Drawn speaking at a cluster of microphones inside the Capitol, in his signature white shirtsleeves and tie with no suit jacket, short brown-grey hair, lean wrestler's build; no text.

people.name: Steve Scalise

stories.visual_notes: Over the shoulders of reporters and camera operators (generic, silhouetted) looking at Jordan at the microphones; behind him a tall arched Capitol window frames the lit dome at dusk. A spiral of blank folded ballot slips rises from behind him toward the dome as a symbol of the secret ballot (illustration, not a count). No text, no Scalise figure, no applause or crowd mood beyond press.

stories.name: Senate Republicans keep John Thune as their leader
facts: On Nov. 10, Senate Republicans re-elected Sen. John Thune of South Dakota as their leader without opposition, in a closed-door meeting in the Old Senate Chamber, after the party's midterm losses.
